old_notes: NEW CELL 2026-10-12 (CI5 added 2026-10-11; ruled by MS in pass commenda-italian-recode-2026-10-12). SEGREGATED BY DEFAULT, IN THE JURIST'S WORDS. Mabsut 22, 48: 'wa-idha qala rabb al-mal li'l-mudarib i'mal fihi bi-ra'yika fa-khalatahu bi-malihi thumma ishtara bihi jaza 'ala al-mudaraba ... wa-law lam yaqul lahu i'mal fihi bi-ra'yika kana huwa bi'l-khalt mukhalifan daminan li'l-mal wa'l-ribh lahu wa'l-wadi'a 'alayhi li-butlan hukm al-mudaraba bi-fawat shartiha' - mixing the capital with his own property without the general authority clause makes the mudarib a contravener, liable for the capital, the profit his and the loss on him, the mudaraba lapsing for failure of its condition (that the capital be a trust in his hands, ibid.). VARIANT: under 'i'mal fihi bi-ra'yika' mixing is permitted, and a loss on a purchase made with both funds falls on them in proportion (ibid., 48). Same default as comanda CI5 (Consolat cap. 219); the opposite of the Genoese and Pisan default (commenda CI5). MEDIUM: one school (Hanafi), one jurist, read first-hand. RECODED 2026-10-13 by OF-R0224 (records/RULINGS-latin-hanafi-mixing-tests-2026-10-13.md, ruling 3; ruled by MS): segregated -> commingled, medium, articulated. The row is 'Islamic (Maliki)' (type row); the coding above rested on Hanafi law alone, carried into a Maliki row. MALIKI RULE, THIS ROW'S (Mudawwana 3, 641): the agent who also trades his own money should mix the two funds and buy with both, 'al-sawab min dhalika an yakhlitahuma jami'an thumma yashtari bihima jami'an' (Ibn al-Qasim); the investor not having stipulated it, mixing attracts no liability, 'la tadmanu lahu' (Malik); goods bought with both are held pro rata, the qirad's share being its capital and the agent's what he paid. At 645 the agent may mix two investors' qirads without stipulation, 'wa-la daman 'alayhi'. What Maliki law bars is STIPULATING the agent's contribution (641, 647-648), on the ground that the investor 'qad jarra ila nafsihi manfa'at mal ghayr malihi', has drawn to himself the benefit of property not his own (648). HANAFI CONTRAST, NOT THIS ROW'S RULE: in al-Sarakhsi, al-Mabsut 22, the mudarib who mixes the capital with his own property without 'i'mal fihi bi-ra'yika' becomes liable for it and the mudaraba lapses for that sum (48), because mixing amounts to consuming the owner's property or to imposing on it a partnership he has not consented to (132-133; the second ground alone at 39); constructive mixing by one purchase with both funds is no breach (48, 133). Title extinction by mixing is Abu Hanifa's view; Abu Yusuf and Muhammad give the owner an option of co-ownership (ruling 1 of the same record). Hanafi law is the only tradition read that segregates by default, and no row codes it: the mudaraba type row is left uncoded. [CORRECTION to the note above: 'Same default as comanda CI5 (Consolat cap. 219)' is superseded; comanda CI5 is commingled on cap. 215 since ruling 29 of 2026-10-12.] MEDIUM: one school, one text (Ibn al-Qasim reporting Malik), read on a transcription; the Muwatta' (Kitab al-qirad) has no rule on mixing, and al-Shafi'i states none in the passages read (al-Umm, qirad sections; Mukhtasar al-Muzani, al-qirad). CONSEQUENCE: every commenda-family row that speaks on CI5 now commingles by default; the family no longer separates on CI5.

What Maliki law bars is STIPULATING the agent's contribution (641, 647-648), on the ground that the investor «قَدْ جَرَّ إلَى نَفْسِهِ مَنْفَعَةَ مَالٍ غَيْرِ مَالِهِ» 'qad jarra ila nafsihi manfa'at mal ghayr malihi', has drawn to himself the benefit of property not his own (648). HANAFI CONTRAST, NOT THIS ROW'S RULE: in al-Sarakhsi, al-Mabsut 22, the mudarib who mixes the capital with his own property without 'i'mal fihi bi-ra'yika' becomes liable for it and the mudaraba lapses for that sum (48), because mixing amounts to consuming the owner's property or to imposing on it a partnership he has not consented to (132-133; the second ground alone at 39); constructive mixing by one purchase with both funds is no breach (48, 133). Title extinction by mixing is Abu Hanifa's view; Abu Yusuf and Muhammad give the owner an option of co-ownership (ruling 1 of the same record). Hanafi law is the only tradition read that segregates by default, and no row codes it: the mudaraba type row is left uncoded. [CORRECTION to the note above: 'Same default as comanda CI5 (Consolat cap. 219)' is superseded; comanda CI5 is commingled on cap. 215 since ruling 29 of 2026-10-12.] MEDIUM: one school, one text (Ibn al-Qasim reporting Malik), read on a transcription; the Muwatta' (Kitab al-qirad) has no rule on mixing, and al-Shafi'i states none in the passages read (al-Umm, qirad sections; Mukhtasar al-Muzani, al-qirad). CONSEQUENCE: every commenda-family row that speaks on CI5 now commingles by default; the family no longer separates on CI5.
